topic: Comparing Planets in the Solar System
key_concepts: The solar system is composed of the Sun and eight planets
The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune
Inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars
Inner planets are small, rocky, solid, and closer to the Sun
Outer planets are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune
Outer planets are large gas giants made mostly of hydrogen and helium
The asteroid belt separates the inner planets from the outer planets
Earth is the only planet known to support life because it has water and a suitable atmosph
Jupiter is the largest planet and has the Great Red Spot
Saturn has the most extensive and complex ring system
Uranus and Neptune are also called ice giants
Planets differ in distance from the Sun, size, temperature, and composition
